overview: This Senate resolution condemns the Chinese government, led by the Chinese Communist Party, for persecuting religious minorities, including Christians, Uyghur and Hui Muslims, and Tibetan Buddhists. It focuses on the October 2025 detention of Pastor Ezra Jin Mingri, founder of the unregistered Zion Church, along with dozens of church members, and calls for their immediate release. It also calls on China to stop harassing church members' relatives, including abroad, to free other detained religious believers, and to respect freedom of religion. It reaffirms the U.S. commitment to promoting religious freedom worldwide. The Senate approved an amended version by voice vote on November 7, 2025. It expresses the Senate's views and does not change any law or impose sanctions.
for: Supporters say the resolution puts the Senate firmly on record against the detention of religious leaders in China and stands with persecuted believers of all faiths.
against: Critics say the resolution is symbolic and does not impose any sanctions or other concrete consequences on those responsible.
